searchText: Anyone else seeing issues w/ erigon/teku on goerli/prater? Seems like our pairs are spinning on waiting for each other for something. Running `thorax/erigon:v2022.07.04` and `teku:22.7.0` Erigon: ``` [INFO] [08-11|02:07:44.459] RPC Daemon notified of new headers from=7382819 to=7382820 header sending=13.767µs log sending=280ns [INFO] [08-11|02:07:44.459] [1/16 Headers] Waiting for Beacon Chain... ``` Teku: ``` 2022-08-11 02:07:40.339 INFO - Slot Event *** Slot: 3639638, Block: ... empty, Justified: 113734, Finalized: 113733, Peers: 70 2022-08-11 02:07:44.526 WARN - Unable to import blocks because execution client is offline. 2022-08-11 02:07:49.615 WARN - Unable to import blocks because execution client is offline. ``` ^ FWIW took awhile but started progressing again Wonder what client is on a diff fork given the low vote rates Could you share full Erigon's log please? Also, there was a bug in Erigon version v2022.07.04. It's better to use v2022.08.01. I appear to have proposed an invalid block with a Lighthouse/Erigon combo. Erigon `devel` , `git_branch=alpha git_tag=v2021.10.03-1610-g7dabdc326-dirty git_commit=7dabdc3269f1e3b098fee5ab4d96ec843823a6fd` https://goerli.beaconcha.in/block/3639696 Logs around the time of that block, if I am reading the UTC right Erigon had a bug with transaction indexing in v2022.07.04, which we fixed in v2022.08.01. But your node is v2022.08.01, right? Let me just verify that was the actual version. I think it wasn't. One sec. I restarted this a few times, it'd grab from `alpha` each time OK yep that was the version, the one linked above. Whatever that commit translates to. It is weird that the tag has a date that is almost an year in the past I think that's a build artefact with how they do the alpha docker images `thorax/erigon alpha b87a9f82686b 5 days ago 643MB` So that'd be v2022.08.01, yes There is no release with that fix yet It was not included We decided not to do a released with it since we wanted to test it, and then i think we forgot <@687974325072035882> Can you confirm that the version of Erigon from the Goerli release returns SYNCING if merge transition payload is build atop of a side fork block? If with that, you refer to the Terminal block then yes Yeah, a terminal block from a side fork, i.e. the one that hasn't been executed. You have mentioned previously that this logic has been patched to be capable of responding VALID/INVALID Below PoS we return SYNCING No, that was downloading blocks on the fly, that other one is still being worked on To clarify: ``` A <- CANONICAL_TB // This is the HEAD \ <- SIDE_FORK_TB <- TRANSITION_PAYLOAD ``` What Erigon version from the Goerli release respond to `newPayload(TRANSITION_PAYLOAD)` given the above state of the client? If PoW block are involved we dont count them as side forks and just return SYNCING/ACCEPTED Got it, thanks Could that be the reason of the stall btw? Erigon process terminal blocks but could not process pos Another thing i noticed was that the issue presented with Teku Yes, if CL sees SYNCING response on `newPayload(mergeTransitionPayload)` it will wait for 128 slots to call `fcU` with this block and proceed with processing this chain What do you mean by "process terminal blocks" in this context? The last PoW block Which should be accessible by all clients pre merge anyway Perhaps <@687974325072035882> can correct me, but my understanding here is different: erigon sends SYNCING/ACCEPTED for the POW TTD block which is not in PoS. So the CL will not send a `notify_newPayload(terminal_block)` for this block since it is not execution enabled. Then if the CL wants to sync the merge block in that branch it will send a `notify_newPayload(mergeBlock)`, Erigon is stuck cause it hasn't executed the parent TTD block. Do they also return SYNCING here? or is it VALID/INVALID? this is now a PoS block. Okay if a side fork have a PoW block in it (like a new terminal block) we dont validate it
